# Packaged Chronicle enum observations

`profile.json` is generated by the opt-in [.NET harness](capture/Program.cs), not
hand-derived JSON. It captures Chronicle **19.29.4**, Fundamentals **7.19.6** and
.NET/System.Text.Json **10.0.12**. [Provenance](provenance.json) identifies the
sources, declarations, isolation and observation format.

This is test evidence, **not implemented Go enum support or a public API
approval**. Ordinary Go tests read the frozen JSON and source pins using only the
standard library. They do not run .NET, Node, package restoration or network I/O.

## What runs

The harness executes the packaged `ChronicleClient.InitializeJsonSerializationOptions`
method by reflection on an uninitialized client, supplying only its options and
naming-policy fields. This isolates the actual configuration method without
running a client constructor, type discovery, connection or disposal. There is
no copied-converter-list fallback.

It then invokes the **actual `EventSerializer` constructor**, supplying empty
artifacts and an explicit empty derived catalog. The unused artifact activator is
null. An event-registry proxy fails every call; its counter is checked outside
all observation catches, so accidentally swallowed registry access invalidates
the entire capture. Both `Serialize` and `Deserialize(Type, JsonObject)` execute.
This is not a claim to have initialized a complete client or event store.

Both naming policies have independent captures of:

- Client, event and schema converter order and serializer settings.
- `Generate(Type)` and `GenerateForReadModel(Type)` outputs, including errors.
- Typed reads, independent writes and separately recorded reserialization.
- Actual packaged `ExpandoObjectConverter` JSON-to-CLR and CLR-to-JSON directions.

The last item is an **in-memory schema conversion**, not BSON or live-kernel
persistence. No Mongo converter, kernel or database runs here.

## Read an observation

Case identity is naming policy, declared type, operation, optional schema API and
ID. `input` for a read is the original JSON text; successful typed `output`
snapshots preserve enum identity and exact decimal value. Serialized outputs are
JSON strings, retaining property order and spelling. Exceptions contain only
categories, never messages or stacks. An accepted read with a failed
`reserialize` is not a successful round trip.

The six historical enum declarations and `PlainConcept` are unchanged from the
[Fundamentals source-corpus harness](https://github.com/Cratis/Fundamentals.Go/blob/b4100a0d791fa370336a87d5fdca5b00d9d47c10/ContractTests/EnumJson/Program.cs).
`Int32Sample`, `AllBits` and the DTOs are separately labelled controls. The
historical 236 observations are neither copied nor replaced: these are new
object-property observations through Chronicle. The newer `e8ac1ec` source
profile and its 42-case supplement are not this package profile.

## Observed boundaries

- Writes are numeric, including undeclared values. Bare numeric reads require a
  declared Int32 value; Bits `5`/`7` fail, while `"A, C"` and `"5"` read as `5`.
  Declared `AB=3` and `All=-1` work; `All=-1` does not admit every numeric input.
  Names are case-insensitive and support the captured whitespace/comma forms.
- Nonnullable scalar null fails. Missing scalar becomes CLR zero, even for
  `NoZero`; missing `Int32Defaults.Value` uses its constructor default `1`.
  Nullable scalar null/missing remains null and is omitted on writing.
- Missing or explicitly null nonnullable arrays normalize to `[]` when read.
  Null array elements fail. An independently constructed null array is omitted
  when written. Nullable array defaults remain null. These are distinct cases,
  not a second constructor invocation standing in for a missing-property read.
- Property policy changes `Value` to `value`; the explicit `explicit_enum` tag
  and acronym `URLValue` remain unchanged. Enum member names are not renamed.
- Int32 schemas carry integer `enum` and aligned `x-enumNames`, **no `int32`
  format**. CLR unsigned ordering places `Max`, `Min`, `Negative` after `0,1` in
  `Int32Sample`. Nullable schemas retain their actual integer/null type array
  without inventing a null enum member or repairing `required`.
- Plain enum schemas agree between the two APIs. `ConceptDefaultControl.Value`
  is only `{"default":null}` in `Generate`; `GenerateForReadModel` restores its
  enum schema. This control does not admit Go enum concepts.
- Expando converts declared integers to names, including array elements.
  Unknown scalar `Bits=5` becomes `"None"` through the outer default fallback;
  unknown nullable scalars disappear, while unknown array elements become null.
  Missing `Int32Defaults.Value` becomes zero in this conversion, not its typed
  constructor default. Do not infer safe read-back from successful conversion.
- Byte/Int64 schema controls fail with `InvalidCastException`; the UInt32 schema
  control emits signed-wrapped high values. These observations do not qualify
  alternate backing types or authorize a schema repair.

The proposed declared-value-only Int32 Go profile is therefore narrower than
some successful C# string reads and writes. It still needs independent evidence
review, implementation tests and an owning kernel/Mongo profile. Do not silently
copy the scalar default fallback into a Go decoder or claim complete equivalence
to either Fundamentals source corpus.

## Reproduce explicitly

Prerequisites: already-installed **SDK 10.0.401** and **runtime 10.0.12**, plus the
locked NuGet dependencies in the normal package cache. SDK and runtime
roll-forward are disabled. No tool or runtime installer is provided. A missing
prerequisite must fail rather than select another runtime.

Run from the repository root. Use a task-owned ignored workspace; on hosts using
`ai-work-lifecycle`, register `enum-profile-capture` before these commands and
retain wanted JSON under its `keep/` directory. The relative paths below are
resolved from `capture/`; build outputs never go into the fixture directory.

```sh
cd serialization/testdata/enum/capture
mkdir -p ../../../../.ai-work/tasks/enum-profile-capture/cache/empty-feed
dotnet restore EnumCapture.csproj --locked-mode \
  --source ../../../../.ai-work/tasks/enum-profile-capture/cache/empty-feed \
  -p:BaseIntermediateOutputPath=../../../../.ai-work/tasks/enum-profile-capture/output/obj/ \
  -p:OutputPath=../../../../.ai-work/tasks/enum-profile-capture/output/bin/
dotnet build EnumCapture.csproj --no-restore -c Release \
  -p:BaseIntermediateOutputPath=../../../../.ai-work/tasks/enum-profile-capture/output/obj/ \
  -p:OutputPath=../../../../.ai-work/tasks/enum-profile-capture/output/bin/
cd ../../../..
dotnet .ai-work/tasks/enum-profile-capture/output/bin/EnumCapture.dll \
  .ai-work/tasks/enum-profile-capture/keep/profile.json
cmp serialization/testdata/enum/profile.json \
  .ai-work/tasks/enum-profile-capture/keep/profile.json
```

The empty feed makes restoration offline: missing cached packages fail. A fresh
machine needs an explicitly authorized normal NuGet restore of the locked
project first. The capture refuses an existing output file; choose a new
filename for another run, never delete retained evidence to satisfy it. It
prints its actual runtime after writing. `cmp` should report no difference on
the captured Arm64 runtime profile; architecture is recorded, not normalized.

Local execution-budget wrappers should run restore, build and capture as
separate bounded phases. The fixture tests are available with
`go test ./serialization -run 'TestEnum(PackageFixture|CaptureSources)'` from the
repository root; they validate evidence structure and selected outcomes, not
.NET execution or Go enum compatibility.
